stories.body: A cargo vessel was hit by an unidentified projectile in the Strait of Hormuz off Oman early Tuesday, according to Britain's UK Maritime Trade Operations agency, as uncertainty persisted over possible US-Iran negotiations. President Donald Trump said talks could begin within days to reopen the strait and address Iran's nuclear programme, calling them Tehran's last chance to avoid an escalation of US strikes. Iran denied that it was negotiating with Washington, saying it was instead discussing a possible temporary commercial-shipping route with Oman. The dispute over access to the strategically vital waterway has become a precondition for wider agreements after renewed fighting spread beyond Iran.
stories.headline: US-Iran talks remain uncertain after a cargo ship is struck in the Strait of Hormuz

stories.body: Ukrainian drone attacks killed at least six people across Russia, with five dead and 10 injured after a strike on an industrial site near Moscow, regional officials said. Fires were reported at warehouse facilities linked to Wildberries, the Russian e-commerce company, near Moscow as well as in the St Petersburg, Tver and Vladimir regions. Kyiv says Wildberries depots help supply Russia's military, an assertion Moscow denies. Russia said it intercepted 320 drones overnight, while Russian strikes in Ukraine killed at least one person in Mykolaiv and injured others, underscoring the continuing exchange of attacks against civilian and industrial areas.
stories.headline: Ukrainian drone strikes kill civilians in Russia and hit Wildberries warehouses

stories.body: Europe's prolonged heat and drought are fuelling wildfires, straining water supplies and disrupting transport, agriculture and power generation. The Rhine has reached record low levels at sites in Germany and the Netherlands, while the Danube and Italy's Po have also fallen sharply, limiting shipping and threatening industrial and agricultural activity. Low Danube levels have forced reduced output at Serbian coal plants and put Hungary's only nuclear plant under pressure, while Romanian manufacturers have agreed to halt production to cut electricity demand. Farmers warn that heat, drought and fires are reducing harvests of vegetables, maize, cereals, grapes and olives, likely pushing food prices higher.
stories.headline: Europe's extreme heat, drought and wildfires disrupt communities, rivers and energy systems

stories.body: Three female lions at Tokyo's Tama Zoological Park have died of suspected heat-related illness after suffering dehydration and multiple organ failure during Japan's punishingly humid summer, while several other lions remain under treatment. Parts of Japan have recently exceeded 40C, and more than 43,000 people have been hospitalised for heatstroke this summer. Extreme temperatures are also worsening conditions in Kumamoto prefecture after last week's magnitude 7.1 earthquake, which killed 38 people. More than 46,000 households remain without water and over 8,500 people are sheltering in crowded facilities, many without air conditioning, as authorities warn of heightened heat-related risks.
stories.headline: Japan's heatwave kills three lions at a Tokyo zoo as earthquake recovery is hampered by high temperatures

stories.body: A coalition of 25 Democratic-led states has sued the Trump administration to block new tariffs imposed on dozens of trading partners over alleged failures to prevent imports made with forced labour. The states argue that the levies, which range from 10% to 12.5% and affect more than 99% of US imports, are an unlawful attempt to replace broad tariffs the Supreme Court struck down in February. The administration invoked Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974, saying it provides lawful authority to respond to unfair trade practices. The lawsuit seeks to halt the tariffs and secure refunds for importers.
stories.headline: US states sue to block Trump's sweeping new tariffs

stories.body: Wildfires driven by drought, extreme heat and strong winds have destroyed hundreds of homes and other structures around Spokane, Washington, prompting mass evacuations in what officials described as the city's worst natural disaster. Reports put the number of damaged or destroyed structures between at least 600 and as many as 1,100, while roughly 60,000 to 65,000 people were forced to leave their homes. Firefighters made progress against several blazes on Monday, and authorities arrested a Spokane man accused of starting one of the fires as residents waited at checkpoints to assess damage, collect medicine and care for pets.
stories.headline: Spokane wildfires force mass evacuations as authorities arrest an arson suspect

stories.body: Michigan Democrats are voting in a closely watched Senate primary between progressive candidate Abdul El-Sayed and Representative Haley Stevens, an establishment-backed congresswoman, to replace retiring Senator Gary Peters. The winner will face Republican former representative Mike Rogers in a crucial contest for Senate control. The race has become a test of whether progressives can win statewide in a battleground state, after El-Sayed drew backing from Bernie Sanders and Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez while Stevens received substantial support from pro-Israel groups, including about $30 million in spending by AIPAC. Michigan's simultaneous House primaries are also exposing broader divisions between the party's progressive and centrist wings.
stories.headline: Michigan Democrats vote in a high-stakes Senate primary testing progressive strength

stories.body: Michigan health officials reported the first two confirmed US deaths linked to the current cyclospora outbreak, saying both people had significant underlying health conditions that may have been worsened by intestinal illness and dehydration. Cyclospora is a microscopic parasite that causes cyclosporiasis, often marked by severe watery diarrhoea, and is generally not life-threatening or difficult to treat in otherwise healthy people. The outbreak has produced nearly 7,000 laboratory-confirmed cases across 45 states, while Michigan has recorded more than 11,000 cases and 193 hospitalisations in its broader tally. Officials have linked the outbreak to lettuce imported from Mexico, though preventing infection can be difficult because washing alone may not remove the parasite.
stories.headline: Michigan reports the first two US deaths linked to a cyclospora outbreak

stories.body: EU interior ministers are holding an emergency meeting over the humanitarian and border crisis in Ceuta after tens of thousands of migrants crossed from Morocco last week. Spain says about 2,500 people remain in the enclave after most were returned or left, although Ceuta's authorities put the remaining total higher. Interior Minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska is expected to seek European solidarity and defend Spain's preventive migration policy, while Spain's government criticises fellow EU states for what it calls an unfair and polarising response. Italy, Denmark and 20 other countries demanded rapid EU action, and some governments imposed or advocated Schengen-related restrictions on travel from Spain.
stories.headline: EU interior ministers meet as Spain seeks solidarity after the Ceuta migration crisis

stories.body: Morocco has rejected claims that it used pressure or blackmail in the Ceuta migration crisis, describing itself as a reliable Spanish partner and arguing that migration management is a shared responsibility. A Moroccan Foreign Ministry source said Rabat had warned Spain that a July Supreme Court ruling against immediate returns of migrants intercepted at sea near Ceuta and Melilla would weaken a key deterrent. Morocco said the ruling, amplified by social media and trafficking networks, contributed to the influx, while insisting its coordination with the Spanish government remains close. Moroccan officials say controlling migration costs the country about €500 million annually and requires the deployment of roughly 20,000 security personnel.
stories.headline: Morocco rejects responsibility for the Ceuta migrant influx and cites a Spanish court ruling

stories.body: Spain's social-security rolls surpassed 22.5 million contributors for the first time in July after adding 41,727 people, extending an annual employment increase of 642,562. Registered unemployment nevertheless rose by 19,517 during the month to 2.31 million, although that figure was still 93,107 lower than a year earlier and the lowest recorded for July since 2007. The government said the monthly increase was unusual and partly reflected changes from labour-market reforms. Employment among foreign workers rose especially strongly, with 262,475 migrants regularised through the government's extraordinary process registered with social security by 30 July.
stories.headline: Spain reaches a record 22.5 million social-security contributors despite a July rise in unemployment

stories.body: Spain's Ibex 35 crossed 20,000 points for the first time on Tuesday, reaching a historic milestone after closing the previous session at a record 19,982. The index was lifted by falling oil prices, improved risk appetite and strong corporate results, particularly from banks and multinationals. The benchmark has risen by almost 39% over the past year despite geopolitical tensions, and its advance came as other major European markets also traded near records. Investors remain focused on developments in the Middle East and the possibility of an agreement that could secure shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.
stories.headline: Spain's Ibex 35 rises above 20,000 points for the first time

stories.body: An indefinite strike by Groundforce staff at Barcelona-El Prat airport has begun to disrupt flights, with about 10 cancellations and at least eight delays reported on Tuesday despite government-mandated minimum services. Two Lufthansa flights to Frankfurt departed without passengers' luggage. The CGT union, which represents workers in ground handling, check-in, boarding and flight coordination, says the walkout responds to deteriorating safety, workload and health conditions among the 1,179 affected workers. Groundforce serves numerous airlines at both terminals, and passengers have been urged to check flight information and allow extra time at the airport.
stories.headline: Ground-handling strike at Barcelona-El Prat causes flight cancellations and delays

stories.body: Catalonia is under warnings for intense rainfall and thunderstorms after a cooler front ended the latest episode of extreme heat but made the atmosphere more unstable. Meteocat has issued rain alerts for around 20 counties, with torrential downpours capable of delivering more than 20 litres per square metre in 30 minutes and possibly bringing hail. The most severe warnings are focused on parts of Ripollès, Garrotxa and Osona, while civil protection has activated a pre-alert for flooding. In Barcelona, showers and storms are expected to remain more likely in nearby inland and pre-coastal areas, while the city is forecast to stay hot, humid and largely dry.
stories.headline: Catalonia braces for torrential rain and thunderstorms after intense heat

stories.body: The Mossos d'Esquadra have begun distributing 1,000 portable metal detectors to police stations across Catalonia to help officers identify concealed knives and other metallic weapons. The devices will be used during patrols, police checks and access screening at major sporting, music and trade-fair events, allowing less invasive searches than manual pat-downs. Police said they will not be used indiscriminately but where there are indications of risk, and that they can also help locate discarded metal objects in public spaces. Distribution will begin in metropolitan Barcelona under the force's Plan Daga, aimed at reducing knife carrying and use in public.
stories.headline: Mossos distribute 1,000 metal detectors to strengthen knife and weapon checks

stories.body: A high-mountain wildfire near Senet in Alta Ribagorça remains active after burning about 80 hectares since Friday, despite rain and thunderstorms that helped firefighters on Monday. Fire crews have asked hikers and other mountain users to avoid the area as they monitor the blaze and the possibility of further weather fronts. Civil Protection lifted a temporary confinement and access restriction covering roughly 2,500 hectares around the fire on Monday night after conditions improved, but authorities say the rainfall was insufficient to extinguish it. Around 30 hectares affected lie within the peripheral protection area of Aigüestortes i Estany de Sant Maurici National Park.
stories.headline: A wildfire in Senet remains active as firefighters ask hikers to avoid the area
